title: Org Admin & Access Requests: intake routing, prioritization ladder, and evaluation rubric
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: establish a repeatable intake & prioritization process for admin and access management requests (RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, org-level policies) so that we can consistently route, scope, and commit work across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope: covers new admin roles and permissions requests, SSO/SAML connector requests, SCIM provisioning flows, org policy requests (e.g., data residency, audit logging), and entitlements requirements from enterprise customers. Excludes bug reports and operational incidents (those go to support/incident triage).

Deliverables:
- Intake form template and routing matrix for triage (self-serve + PM gate)
- Prioritization ladder/rubric with weighted criteria (security risk, compliance exposure, ARR / number of customers, code complexity, cross-team dependencies)
- Triage playbook with SLA targets for initial response and expected time-to-scope
- Example decision logs and canned responses for sales/CS to manage expectations
- Integration points: create tags in Zendesk, auto-create Linear issue with labels, and dashboard to track backlog/fallout
notes: 2026-02-10: Ticket created after synthesis of 6 enterprise intake interviews (Sales, CS, 3 F500 customers). Common asks: SCIM provisioning for multiple orgs, per-org RBAC models, SSO with vendor-specific claims mapping.

2026-02-18: Discovery complete. Proposed prioritization criteria: (1) customer impact (num customers, ARR), (2) security/compliance risk, (3) implementation complexity (engineering estimate), (4) long-term platform value (reusability). Working weights proposed: 30/25/20/25.

2026-02-25: Design review — DES-412 provided two intake form mockups. Feedback from design: reduce free-text fields, add conditional flows for SSO vs SCIM to cut triage time. Action: Liam to pick one mockup and validate with 2 CS reps.

2026-03-03: Engineering scoping session with ENG infra team. Initial estimate for baseline SCIM onboarding flow = 5 sprint-weeks if built as platform feature; 2 weeks to implement one-off customer connector. Engineering recommends creating a 'platform-first' flag to prefer reusable work for P0/P1 requests.

2026-03-06: Security review (SEC-112) flagged multi-tenant SCIM provisioning design. Decision: require threat model sign-off for any design that writes org-level role mappings. Added security_review_required = true.

2026-03-09: PM sync with Sales and CS. Agreed SLAs: initial triage within 3 business days for enterprise customers; target time-to-scope published as 2 weeks for P0/P1 and 6-8 weeks for P2. CS to include expected handoff doc in support ticket.

2026-03-11: Implemented routing matrix prototype in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Access+Request+Routing. Matrix routes to: 'platform initiative' (PM+ENG+DES), 'customer connector' (ENG short-lived), 'policy exception' (Legal+Security), or 'defer to product backlog'.

2026-03-12: Created dashboard to track intake volumes and SLA compliance: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/access-requests. Early metrics show ~12 access requests/month with 25% labeled as 'custom connector' and 40% as 'policy change'.

2026-03-13: Action items: (1) Finalize intake form and embed in Sales/CS playbook (owner: Liam). (2) Create automation to create Linear issue with labels and pre-filled fields from form (owner: SRE team, ENG-2345). (3) Draft PRD for baseline SCIM + RBAC primitives (owner: Maya).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form implemented and linked from Sales/CS playbook
Automated Linear issue creation with at least: key, customer name, request type (RBAC/SSO/SCIM/Policy), estimated impact, and triage labels
Prioritization rubric documented and used for 2 pilot customer requests
SLA targets published and dashboard tracking SLA compliance
Security threat-model checklist added to process and Security sign-off required for P0 requests
